_about: Button facts from the HIG Buttons page (CRITICAL for this skill). Every value carries a source tag: HIG = stated by Apple on the page · WCAG = W3C · CONV = apple-skill convention (Apple gives no number) · FN = Nonplo field note. Colours come from apple-system-colors.css; the page itself gives no colour values.

minimum.note: general rule: at least 44 x 44 pt so a fingertip, pointer, eyes or remote can select it

target.note: 44 x 44 CSS px hit region on touch-width layouts; the visible button may be smaller if the hit region is extended (padding or ::after)

floor.note: WCAG 2.5.8 minimum for pointer layouts; between 24 and 44 is a WARN

web.probeRule: FAIL below 44 at 375 px viewport width; FAIL below 24 at any width; WARN 24-43 at desktop width

press.text: Always include a press state for a custom button; without it the button feels unresponsive.

prominentPerView.text: Keep the number of prominent buttons to one or two per view; more raises cognitive load.

distinguishBy.text: Same-size buttons signal a coherent set; different sizes near each other look inconsistent. Highlight the preferred option with a more prominent style.

labelColour.text: Avoid a label colour similar to bright content-layer backgrounds; prefer the default monochromatic label (Liquid Glass colour).

fieldNote.text: Nonplo principle 4: exactly one filled button per screen; black pill on light / white pill on dark; destructive secondary = red text, no fill.

purpose.text: Each button clearly communicates its purpose with an icon, a text label, or both.

familiarIcons.web: Lucide/Phosphor/Ionicons glyph; never SF Symbols artwork on the web

label.text: A few words describing what the button does; consider starting with a verb ("Add to Cart"); Apple specifies title-style capitalisation.
label.webNote: Skill decision 2026-09-29: follow Apple, Title Case for button labels (see writing.md capitalisation table). Nonplo's sentence-case convention is set aside for now.

iconOnlyName.text: An icon-only button needs an accessible name (aria-label / visually hidden text); macOS and visionOS also show a tooltip after hover or dwell (HIG note).

roles.primary: The default button, the one people are most likely to choose; uses the accent colour; responds to Return; in a sheet/alert/editable view it lets the view close on Return.
roles.destructive: Performs an action that can destroy data; uses the system red colour.
rules: Assign the primary role to the button people are most likely to choose.
Never assign the primary role to a destructive button, even if it is the most likely choice (people press a prominent button without reading).

illustration.destructive: red label on a neutral fill

activityIndicator.text: Configure a button to show an activity indicator (spinner) for an action that does not complete instantly; optionally change the label ("Checkout" → "Checking out…"); the indicator replaces the button image, sits on the leading side of the label.
activityIndicator.web: aria-busy="true" + spinner glyph aria-hidden + changed label text + prevent double submit (aria-disabled)

pushButton.text: Standard button; text, symbol, icon or image, or both; can be default; can be tinted.

flexibleHeight.text: Only for tall or variable-height content (two lines of text, tall icon); same corner radius and padding as a push button.

ellipsis.text: Append a trailing ellipsis to the title when the button opens another window, view or app (more input is needed).

springLoading.text: Consider spring loading (drag over + force click) on Magic Trackpad systems.

squareButton.text: Symbol/icon only (no label), in or beneath the view it affects; not in a toolbar or status bar (use a toolbar item); prefer an SF Symbol.

placement.location: lower corner opposite the dismissal buttons, vertically aligned with them

imageButton.paddingNote: about 10 pixels between image edges and button edges (the edges define the clickable area)
imageButton.label: below the image button

visionOS.backgroundShape: Prefer a discernible background shape and fill (exceptions: toolbar, context menu, alert, ornament).
visionOS.avoid: No custom button with white fill and black text/icon; the system reserves it for the toggled state.

spacing.note: Avoid small or mini buttons in a vertical stack or horizontal row.

visionOS.sound: Buttons play sound as feedback; the system doesn't play haptics; use standard controls for the known sounds.

watchOS.material: inline buttons gain a contrasting material effect
watchOS.toolbar: put buttons in the corners with a toolbar; the system moves time and title and applies Liquid Glass
watchOS.primaryActions: full-width buttons; if two share a row use the same height and short titles or images
watchOS.stacks: identical height for vertical stacks of one- and two-line text buttons
watchOS.toolbarButtons: navigation to related areas or contextual actions for the view's content

web.semantics: Use <button> (or <a href> for navigation). A clickable <div>/<span> is not a button: no keyboard, no role, no Return/Space.
web.defaultButton: In a dialog or form the primary action is the default submit button so Enter activates it; a destructive action must never be the default.

focusRing.rule: visible :focus-visible indicator, ≥ 3:1 against adjacent colours (WCAG 2.4.7/1.4.11); never outline:none without a replacement

labelContrast.note: white on system blue #0088FF is 3.52:1 → use a deeper prominent fill (#1E6EF4 4.57, #0040DD 7.6) or a black/white pill (FN).

spacing.note: adjacent standalone buttons keep ≥ 8 px between hit regions; attached groups (segmented, toolbar, tablist) are exempt

web.hitRegionTrick: keep the visual size (e.g. 36 px pill) and extend the hit region with ::after {inset:-4px} or padding so it measures ≥ 44 px (FN pills are 36/30 px)
